# freedata

**HF messaging and file transfer over codec2 modems, with a browser interface**

- **Version recorded:** 0.18.2
- **Categories:** `emcomm`, `soundcard-modems`
- **Upstream:** <https://freedata.app>
- **Needs first:** `libportaudio2`, `libhamlib-utils`

## What it does

FreeDATA sends messages and files between stations over HF, using the codec2 OFDM data modes: a chat-style inbox, file attachments, beacons, CQ calls and a map of stations heard. It runs as a local server (`freedata`) and you use it in a web browser; by default it serves http://127.0.0.1:5000/gui and opens that page for you. The modem is built in, so there is no separate modem program to start.
**It transmits.** A message, a CQ, a beacon or a ping keys your radio on HF and sends. A licence and the band plan apply. Nothing here keys the rig until you have set up rig control and started FreeDATA yourself; installing it transmits nothing.

## Why you would want it

Keyboard-to-keyboard messaging and file transfer over HF between stations that both run it, with no gateway and no account: station to station, when there is no internet to route through. It is an alternative to VARA's own chat programs and to fldigi's ARQ modes, in a browser interface.
**It is not Winlink.** FreeDATA's protocol is its own. It does not speak to ARDOP, VARA or Mercury stations, Pat does not use it, and it does not reach Winlink gateways. For Winlink over HF, use Pat with ardopcf or Mercury. Upstream has a VARA-style socket interface (ports 9000 and 9001, off by default) that it marks work in progress; it has not been tried with Pat here.

## Before it will work

An SSB transceiver with audio in and out, and a way to key it: rigctld (from hamlib), flrig, a serial PTT line, or VOX, chosen in FreeDATA's settings page. Your callsign and grid square go in the same settings page, which writes `~/.config/FreeDATA/config.ini`; FreeDATA rewrites that file itself, so Hammunition does not template it.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`packet`](../profiles/packet.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install freedata --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

  - The pinned set installed with --require-hashes into a Python 3.13 venv on the field laptop (Parrot 7.3) on 2026-09-30, 219 MB on disk, and `import freedata_server.codec2` loaded the bundled library and listed its twelve modes. The server itself was not started here: it opens the audio devices through PortAudio on startup.

## Known problems

**A fresh configuration carries upstream's example callsign, AA1AAA, and grid JN48ea.** Replace both in Settings before you transmit anything: the first start copies upstream's example file into `~/.config/FreeDATA/config.ini` as it is.
**Any web page open in the same browser can drive it.** The server allows cross-origin requests from every origin (`allow_origins=["*"]`) and has no login, and its API includes calls that transmit (`/modem/cqcqcq`, `/modem/beacon`, `/modem/send_test_frame`). That was read from upstream's server and modem API modules (freedata_server, server and api.modem) at 0.18.2 and not tested here. Run the server while you are using it, stop it when you are not, and keep `modemaddress` at 127.0.0.1: an empty value makes it listen on every interface.
Upstream's README says development has slowed and that 0.18.x accumulated many changes; if 0.18.2 misbehaves, upstream points at 0.17.8, whose PyPI wheel has no web interface (so it is not the version carried). The two optional reporting features that send your station to api.freedata.app (Explorer and statistics) are off in the default configuration. x86-64 only: the codec2 library FreeDATA ships has no Linux arm64 build. The window, the audio path and a transmission have not been exercised from this install.

## Keeping it current

- probe: pypi
- strategy: reinstall
- A few releases a year (0.17.6 to 0.17.8 in 2025, 0.18.0 to 0.18.2 in July 2026). Re-run the uv compile for the new version and check the wheel still carries freedata_gui/dist and lib/codec2/libcodec2.so.

## Where to get help with the software itself

DJ2LS and contributors. GitHub issues at https://github.com/DJ2LS/FreeDATA and the wiki at wiki.freedata.app. GPL-3.0 LICENSE file read at tag v0.18.2 on 2026-09-30; the bundled libcodec2 is codec2's LGPL-2.1 library.
